newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian shares end week up, bull run set to stay.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian shares end week up, bull run set to stay.

text.p: Shares ended higher on the Nigerian stock exchange on Friday and were set to stretch their current rally into another week, traders said.
The all-share index closed at 8413.13 from 8336.91 on Thursday, buoyed by strong blue chip gains, they said.
"The index would have risen by a higher margin but for the stagnant position of oil marketing shares," one trader said.
Oil marketing shares were unchanged for the second consecutive day on Friday as fuel shortage persisted in Lagos.
Because of this the market did not react to full year result of Total TOTL.LG posted on Friday, analysts said.

The company said after-tax profit slid to 837.8 million naira by end-1996 from 1.1 billion naira a year ago. It proposed a dividend of two naira and a bonus share issue of one-for-six against five naira in 1995.
In the absence of much action in the oil sector, food and beverages shares took the leading position.
Coca-Cola bottlers Nigerian Bottling Company and Nestle eached gained 50 kobo to 50.50 naira and 66.50 naira, respectively.
Hefty advances were also recorded by Nigeria's four leading banks, dealers said.
Afribank, the fourth largest, was up 20 kobo at 8.50 naira, the same as UBA which closed at 13.30 naira.
First Bank maintained its leading position with a 60 kobo rise to 18.00 naira as investors rushed to consolidate their holding in anticipation of an improved corporate performance.
Conglomerates did well with UAC at 14.50 naira and Lever Brothers at 25.25 naira, ahead of the rest with a 40 kobo advance apiece.
Tyre maker Dunlop soared 60 kobo to 12.90 naira in reaction to its satisfactory full year result posted last week.
Traders said Dunlop especially and other blue chips looked set to rise next week on an expected increase in demand. "There is nothing on the horizon to halt the bull run," said one.
Few stocks have fallen recently. Among these are Benue Cement Company which dipped again on Friday, closing four kobo lower at 5.59 naira.
Stationery firm Tripple Gee also fell 10 kobo on profit-taking to end at 5.20 naira.
